literal: we see each other from after
usage: This is the most common and natural way to say 'see you later' in Moroccan Darija. It is used in both casual and semi-formal contexts among friends, family, and colleagues. The verb form implies a mutual 'we will see each other', making it appropriate regardless of the gender or number of people you are addressing.

variants.label: To one person (I will see you)
variants.note: Used when you want to say 'I will see you' rather than 'we will see each other', addressing either a man or a woman.

variants.label: To a group (I will see you all)
variants.english: I will see you all later.
variants.note: The plural form of 'I will see you', used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: Casual / Short
variants.note: A very common, abbreviated way to say goodbye meaning 'until later'.

examples.arabic: خصني نمشي دابا، نتشاوفو من بعد.
examples.transliteration: khssni nmshi daba, ntshawfou mn b3d.
examples.english: I have to go now, see you later.
Alright I'll leave you be, see you later.

examples.english: We will talk tonight, see you later.
